content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text makes the Isaiah 7:14 almah/bethulah word-count ambiguity a ground for UNDERDETERMINED rather than treating a two-sense verse as not open.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.","rule_words":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse.","room":"'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.' I weighed whether 'the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways' leaves the verse open as UNDERDETERMINED or whether both senses stand and it is not open.","why":"The judge uses the fact that the almah/bethulah word-count 'cuts both ways' as a basis for UNDERDETERMINED, contrary to K-S2's command that a two-sense verse is not open and both senses stand."}
